evals.prompt: Our client opened https://example.com/sitemap.xml and says it looks broken: the whole file is a few endless lines of XML that nobody can read. Search Console says the sitemap is fine. What is going on and how do we make it look clean?
evals.expected_output: An answer that separates the two readers: the file is valid for robots (Search Console says Success) and only needs an elegant layout for people. It runs or asks for sitemap_audit.py, then pretty-prints every file (index and children) as the last build step with sitemap_audit.py --format or xmllint --format: XML declaration on line 1, one element per line, two-space indentation, fixed order inside each entry (loc, lastmod, alternates with x-default last, images), no blank lines. It does not add an XSL stylesheet, CSS, a script or an HTML layer, and it explains that the browser's raw XML view is the expected rendering. Acceptance: audit exit 0, xmllint --format diff empty, view-source shows the clean layout, Search Console Success with an unchanged URL count.

evals.prompt: Our multilingual site has a single sitemap.xml of 1.4 MB with 1,800 URLs in 5 languages, hreflang links on every URL, priority and changefreq everywhere, and 700 location pages that all show the same lastmod. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: An answer that says the file is valid (under 50,000 URLs and 50 MB) but heavy and partly dishonest: split it into a sitemap index with children by section and language so Search Console reports indexation per template; remove priority and changefreq, which Google ignores; replace the shared lastmod (a generation date) with the real content change date, since Google ignores inaccurate lastmod; keep hreflang in one place or generate the sitemap and head versions from the same table, and check the same page count per language. It points to sitemap_audit.py for the measured version and does not invent numbers it was not given.

evals.prompt: Our sitemap has an XSL stylesheet and since Chrome updated there is a red banner saying the site uses XSLT which will soon be removed. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: An answer that recommends removing the stylesheet entirely: delete the xml-stylesheet instruction from every sitemap file, delete the XSL and any xslt-polyfill file, and keep the raw XML pretty-printed (identical to xmllint --format, one element per line, two-space indentation). It explains the banner (Chrome removes native XSLT on 17 November 2026), notes that robots ignored the stylesheet so nothing changes for them, does not suggest a polyfill or any HTML layer, and checks the result with sitemap_audit.py (no stylesheet or script finding) and Search Console (Success, same URL count).
